blocks.value: A **data type** specifies a set of values and their operations. Values have particular data types because they are stored in memory in the same format and have the same operations defined for them.
**Primitive data types** are the fundamental data types in Java: predefined by the language and named by a keyword.
The same characters can mean different things depending on the type. The type decides what operations are allowed and what they do. With numbers, `+` adds. With text, `+` joins:

System.out.println(5 + 5);        // 10, two int values
System.out.println("5" + "5");    // 55, two String values
